Topics · Meaning and purpose

Why can't I stop scrolling my phone?

The Quran's name for it is older than phones: the race for more. It gives hope and free time a direction.

Part 1 of 3

﴿بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ أَلْهَىٰكُمُ ٱلتَّكَاثُرُ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Competition in [worldly] increase diverts you

Quran · At-Takathur 102:1

Translation

Woe to those who join house to house, who lay field to field, until there is no room, and you are made to dwell alone in the middle of the land!

Original · Hebrew

ה֗וֹי מַגִּיעֵ֥י בַ֨יִת֙ בְּבַ֔יִת שָׂדֶ֥ה בְשָׂדֶ֖ה יַקְרִ֑יבוּ עַ֚ד אֶ֣פֶס מָק֔וֹם וְהֽוּשַׁבְתֶּ֥ם לְבַדְּכֶ֖ם בְּקֶ֥רֶב הָאָֽרֶץ׃

Isaiah · 5:8

World English Bible

The feeling has a name in the Quran, and it is older than phones. The first verse of a short chapter says: the race for more has kept you occupied. More views, more followers, more of everything, until attention is spent without being given anywhere. The text does not scold you for being tired. It names the machine you are inside: a rivalry for more that never says enough.

A question for you

How do you feel after scrolling?

If you sayTired.
ThenTiredness is an honest signal from attention that has been spent.
If you sayLonely.
ThenMany feel that among so many people. The next two passages speak of what fills.
If you sayFine. It is just a habit.
ThenThen the next questions may interest you with no pressure. They are about direction, not about banning.

Part 2 of 3

﴿ٱلْمَالُ وَٱلْبَنُونَ زِينَةُ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا ۖ وَٱلْبَـٰقِيَـٰتُ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتُ خَيْرٌ عِندَ رَبِّكَ ثَوَابًا وَخَيْرٌ أَمَلًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

Wealth and children are [but] adornment of the worldly life. But the enduring good deeds are better to your Lord[792] for reward and better for [one's] hope.

Translator's notes

[792] i.e., in His sight or evaluation.

Quran · Al-Kahf 18:46

Translation

“Don’t lay up treasures for yourselves on the earth, where moth and rust consume, and where thieves break through and steal; but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust consume, and where thieves don’t break through and steal; for where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.

Original · Ancient Greek

Μὴ θησαυρίζετε ὑμῖν θησαυροὺς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ὅπου σὴς καὶ βρῶσις ἀφανίζει, καὶ ὅπου κλέπται διορύσσουσιν καὶ κλέπτουσιν· θησαυρίζετε δὲ ὑμῖν θησαυροὺς ἐν οὐρανῷ, ὅπου οὔτε σὴς οὔτε βρῶσις ἀφανίζει, καὶ ὅπου κλέπται οὐ διορύσσουσιν οὐδὲ κλέπτουσιν· ὅπου γάρ ἐστιν ὁ θησαυρός σου, ἐκεῖ ἔσται καὶ ἡ καρδία σου.

the Gospel (Matthew) · 6:19-21

World English Bible

The Quran does not tell you to throw away what is bright. It calls it adornment: wealth and children are the decoration of this life. Decoration is allowed to be lovely. But the verse adds what lasts, the enduring good deeds, which it says are better with your Lord for reward and better for hope. Hope is the word. If you scroll to feel hopeful and end up emptier, the verse says where hope lives.

A question for you

What gives you something to lean toward?

If you sayA person.
ThenPeople are the oldest and most lasting of hopes.
If you sayA skill I am building.
ThenMastery lasts, and belongs among the lasting things when goodness goes with it.
If you sayA purpose bigger than me.
ThenThat is the direction of the next passage.

Part 3 of 3

﴿فَإِذَا فَرَغْتَ فَٱنصَبْ٧ وَإِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ فَٱرْغَب٨﴾

Translation of the meaning

So when you have finished [your duties], then stand up [for worship]. And to your Lord direct [your] longing.

Quran · Ash-Sharh 94:7-8

Translation

Yes, in the way of your judgments, Yahweh, we have waited for you. Your name and your renown are the desire of our soul. With my soul I have desired you in the night. Yes, with my spirit within me I will seek you earnestly; for when your judgments are on the earth, the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness.

Original · Hebrew

אַ֣ף אֹ֧רַח מִשְׁפָּטֶ֛יךָ יְהוָ֖ה קִוִּינ֑וּךָ לְשִׁמְךָ֥ וּֽלְזִכְרְךָ֖ תַּאֲוַת־נָֽפֶשׁ׃ נַפְשִׁ֤י אִוִּיתִ֨יךָ֙ בַּלַּ֔יְלָה אַף־רוּחִ֥י בְקִרְבִּ֖י אֲשַֽׁחֲרֶ֑ךָּ כִּ֞י כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר מִשְׁפָּטֶ֨יךָ֙ לָאָ֔רֶץ צֶ֥דֶק לָמְד֖וּ יֹשְׁבֵ֥י תֵבֵֽל׃

Isaiah · 26:8-9

World English Bible

A short instruction in the Quran about free time: when you have finished, put in effort again, and turn your longing toward your Lord. It treats the empty space after work as an opening, not a void to fill. The gap between tasks is exactly where the phone appears. The verse puts something there: a turning of the heart. Not a rule about screens. An invitation to aim your wanting.

A question for you

What do you wish your attention were for?

If you sayThe people I love.
ThenAmong the deepest places longing can be aimed.
If you saySomething I am building.
ThenThe verse says: put in effort again. Building is of this kind.
If you saySomething bigger than me.
ThenThat is what the verse calls 'to your Lord'.

The same in the other books

Translation

One grows rich by his diligence and self-denial, and this is the portion of his reward: when he says, “I have found rest, and now I will eat of my goods!” he doesn’t know how much time will pass until he leaves them to others and dies.

Original · Ancient Greek

Ἔστι πλουτῶν ἀπὸ προσοχῆς καὶ σφιγγίας αὐτοῦ, καὶ αὕτη ἡ μερὶς τοῦ μισθοῦ αὐτοῦ. Ἐν τῷ εἰπεῖν αὐτὸν, εὗρον ἀνάπαυσιν, καὶ νῦν φάγωμαι ἐκ τῶν ἀγαθῶν μου, καὶ οὐκ οἶδε τίς καιρὸς παρελεύσεται, καὶ καταλείψει αὐτὰ ἑτέροις, καὶ ἀποθανεῖται.

Sirach · 11:18-19

World English Bible

Translation

“So be careful, or your hearts will be loaded down with carousing, drunkenness, and cares of this life, and that day will come on you suddenly. For it will come like a snare on all those who dwell on the surface of all the earth.

Προσέχετε δὲ ἑαυτοῖς μήποτε βαρηθῶσιν ὑμῶν αἱ καρδίαι ἐν κραιπάλῃ καὶ μέθῃ καὶ μερίμναις βιωτικαῖς, καὶ ἐπιστῇ ἐφʼ ὑμᾶς αἰφνίδιος ἡ ἡμέρα ἐκείνη ὡς παγίς· ἐπεισελεύσεται γὰρ ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς καθημένους ἐπὶ πρόσωπον πάσης τῆς γῆς.

the Gospel (Luke) · 21:34-35

World English Bible

There is no guilt greater than to sanction ambition; no calamity greater than to be discontented with one's lot; no fault greater than the wish to be getting. Therefore the sufficiency of contentment is an enduring and unchanging sufficiency.

Translation

for riches are not forever, nor does the crown endure to all generations.
